posts.content_md:
I wonder why we don't see hologaphic books. That is, a small 1" by 1" square hologram in which you couple with a laser pointer and as you move the pointer in an array fashion of a few mm across and down, you get a whole new page. With a 3mm beam diamter and a each hologram occupying 4mm square on the 1x1 plate, you could easily get 36 pages on a 1x1" square. 

To quadruple that, have 4 pages at a time displayed per 4mm square hologram. That's 144 pages. With just a few of these, you have a full text book. 

Or for you Danny, each of the gospels. Hang the 1" square hologram and the mini laser pointer around your neck and you can read the bible anytime you want. We could call it the Bible Necklace.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
One word. Usability.

You could do what you suggest but you still need a good surface to project the image onto while you read. Plus you need a holder, otherwise you'll get tired of holding the hologram in one hand and the laser in the other. Then there's the fact that every time you put it down you lose your place.

Tackle usability and you'd have something that might catch on.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
That's not usability. That's utility.

Such a thing would be useful but the idea doesn't describe how it's used or how easy it is to use. The latter is the problem with most holographic ideas. The final implementation has some fatal drawback (do *you* carry a halogen light with you all the time?) that prevents it from being adopted by the masses. A holographic reference work, while technically interesting, doesn't beat a small book that fits in your pocket, will hold a bookmark, can be written upon and doesn't take any power beyond that needed to move your fingers in order to turn the pages.

Once you can invert the difference between the two, then you'll have a holographic reference that everyone wants.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
I see.

How about a small laser pointer that fits on your keychain. It has a small disk on the end of it (enclosed in a casing of course to protect it) that has multiple holographic pages on it. Somewhat like the disk on a viewmaster. The casing of the laser pointer has a button on it that clicks over to the next image, somewhat like the viewmaster. Thus you take the laser pointer out of your pocket, turn it on, shine it down on the table top or wall and can click to scroll through the pages. This HoloBook can be used in lighted areas as well as dimly lit or dark areas (in a night club, in a theater, in the back of a cab at night, in a plane, etc). Clicking would be faster then turning pages. And a final sellign point is multiple pages can be on one image, thus allow even faster searching from your eyeballs.

If you have ever seen those laser pointers with interchangable heads that have different projection patterns on them, they are pretty bright. 

Of couse we could alway just imbed all pages on a single hologram that was worn as glasses that would allow you to instantly reference the words that are virtually visible all the time. It would be a static HUD. We would call it the "HUD Language in 5 seconds or less".
